sections.body: Validate observations, remove duplicates, distinguish false positives from accepted risk, identify root cause and affected population, and rate likelihood and impact in context. Reconcile technical severity with business criticality, exploitability, compensating controls, and exposure. Preserve the evidence trail from finding to requirement and owner.
keyPoints: Tool severity is an input, not the final business risk rating.
Uncertainty and limitations belong in the conclusion.
sections.title: Analyze before concluding

sections.body: Technical reports need reproducible evidence and remediation detail; executive summaries need risk, business impact, trends, decisions, and accountable owners. State scope, method, dates, criteria, exceptions, residual risk, and due dates. Avoid absolute claims when sampling or coverage is limited.
keyPoints: Every material finding needs an owner and next action.
Different audiences need different detail, not contradictory conclusions.
Remediation status should be updated and retested.
sections.title: Report for action

sections.body: Remediation should identify root cause, owner, priority, due date, compensating control, validation method, and residual risk. Exception handling should document affected scope, rationale, appropriate approval, residual risk, and a planned review consistent with organizational governance. Ethical disclosure protects affected parties and evidence through authorized coordination, confidentiality, and agreed notification and legal channels.
keyPoints: Closure requires retest or sufficient evidence, not a ticket status.
Exceptions should remain visible and be reconsidered according to the organization’s approved governance.
Disclosure balances harm reduction, legal duty, affected-party notice, and evidence preservation.
sections.title: Turn findings into accountable remediation and ethical disclosure

sections.body: When remediation cannot meet the needed time frame, document the affected asset and control objective, evidence and severity context, accountable risk owner, business justification, compensating controls, residual risk, approval authority, and a planned review or reconsideration condition consistent with organizational governance. Report decision-makers the material risk, alternatives, owner, and deadline; give implementers reproducible technical evidence and the required corrective action.
keyPoints: An exception is a documented, authorized residual-risk decision that must be revisited under organizational governance.
Closure requires evidence that the remediation or compensating control works in the affected environment.
sections.title: Treat an exception as a controlled risk decision, not a closed finding
